title: Incremental loads: a watermark that misses nothing
objectives: Say what a watermark is: the point the last load got up to
Pick a watermark column that only grows, so late rows aren't missed
Work out the next watermark from the rows you loaded, not from the clock

exercises.prompt: Return the rows this load should copy: every row in source_orders that arrived after the last load's watermark. Columns order_id, order_date, amount and arrived_at, smallest order_id first.
hints: load_state holds one row: last_watermark, the arrived_at the last load got up to.
Order 1006 is dated 2026-04-01, before the watermark, but it arrived after it. Should this load copy it?
Filter on arrived_at, the column that only grows, and use > so the last load's rows aren't copied twice.

exercises.prompt: Return the watermark the next load should start from, as one row with one column, next_watermark: the latest arrived_at among the rows this load copies. If it copies nothing, keep last_watermark.
hints: The next load starts where this one ended: the newest arrived_at it copied.
now() is when the query ran, not when the data arrived. A row that lands while the load runs would be skipped for good.
coalesce(max(arrived_at), last_watermark) keeps the old watermark when there's nothing new.
